description: Defends the night as habitat, biological clock, shared sky, and public resource, while taking the safety benefits of electric lighting seriously. Examines nocturnal pollination, sea turtle hatchlings, migratory birds, the loss of visible stars, circadian timing, road safety and crime research, and Flagstaff's lighting policy; argues for light precisely where and when it serves a purpose.
